newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Estonia disaster probe chief quits over lies.
newsitem.headline: Estonia disaster probe chief quits over lies.

text.p: Sweden's chief accident investigator, Olof Forssberg, resigned under pressure on Monday after admitting he had lied about the safety background to the Estonia ferry disaster which cost 852 lives in 1994.
"We have decided that it is best if Forssberg leaves his position," Communications Minister Ines Uusmann told a news conference.

Forssberg was both head of Sweden's official accident commission and the senior Swede on a three-nation commission probing the loss of the roll-on roll-off ferry Estonia in a storm south-west of Finland. He resigned both posts.
The three-nation commission, whose findings could influence law suits brought by survivors and victim's families, has published no official report. It's senior Estonian also resigned last year.
Swedish radio broadcast an interview with Forssberg on Monday in which he said he lied when he said that he had never received a letter discussing the safety of certain types of vessels.
The letter discussed the safety of ramps on "ro-ro" ferries that are supposed to stop water flooding onto such vessels' car decks.
Forssberg said the error he made was a one-off and that it did not cast doubt on the validity of the investigation.
The Estonia's bow visor snapped off in a Baltic storm in September 1994 and a protective ramp collapsed, sending thousands of tonnes of water onto the car deck.
Investigations have unearthed a string of errors , including weaknesses in the structure of the ship and design flaws that allowed water to run to one side of the ship.
